subjective.question: Differentiate between needs, wants and demands with the help of examples.
subjective.answer: A need is a state of felt deprivation, such as the need for food, clothing, shelter, safety and belonging. Needs are a basic part of the human makeup and are not created by marketers. Wants are the form human needs take as they are shaped by culture and individual personality. A person needs food but may want a burger, pizza or biryani depending on his culture and tastes. Demands are human wants that are backed by buying power. When consumers have the money and willingness to pay, their wants become demands, and marketers measure this demand for their products.

subjective.question: Differentiate between the selling concept and the marketing concept.
subjective.answer: Selling concept: It is an inside-out perspective. It starts with the factory, focuses on the company's existing products, and calls for heavy selling and promotion to obtain profitable sales. Its aim is to sell what the company makes rather than making what the market wants. Marketing concept: It is an outside-in perspective. It starts with a well-defined market, focuses on customer needs, coordinates all marketing activities affecting customers, and obtains profits by creating long-term customer relationships based on customer value and satisfaction.

subjective.question: What is marketing myopia? How can a company avoid it?
subjective.answer: Marketing myopia is the mistake of paying more attention to the specific products a company offers than to the benefits and experiences produced by these products. Such companies define their business in narrow product terms (for example, 'we sell shoes') and lose sight of the underlying customer need, so they are caught unprepared when a new technology or competitor serves that need better. A company can avoid marketing myopia by defining its business in market-oriented (need-based) terms rather than product terms, and by keeping its focus on customers' changing needs and wants.

subjective.question: What is the marketing mix? Explain its elements (4 Ps) along with the corresponding 4 Cs.
subjective.answer: The marketing mix is the set of controllable marketing tools that the firm blends to produce the response it wants in the target market. Its four elements, known as the four Ps, are: • Product: the goods-and-services combination the company offers to the target market (customer point of view: Customer needs and wants). • Price: the amount of money customers have to pay to obtain the product (customer point of view: Cost to the customer). • Place: the company activities that make the product available to target consumers (customer point of view: Convenience). • Promotion: the activities that communicate the merits of the product and persuade target customers to buy it (customer point of view: Communication).

subjective.question: What is meant by Market?
subjective.answer: Markets The concepts of exchange and relationships lead to the concept of a market. A market is the set of actual and potential buyers of a product. Originally a market was a place where buyers and sellers gathered to exchange goods (such as a village square). Economists use the term to designate a collection of buyers and sellers who transact in a particular product class (as in the housing market) Marketers see buyers as constituting a market and sellers constituting an industry.

subjective.question: Briefly define customer and consumer?
subjective.answer: A Customer- purchases or pays for products or services A Consumer- is ultimate user of the product or service, the consumer may not have paid for the product or service.

subjective.question: How does an organization create a customer?
subjective.answer: Organizations can create the customers by identifying customer’s needs, designing goods and services that meet those needs then communicating information About those goods and services to prospective buyers. Providing the necessary services and follow-up to ensure customer satisfaction after the purchase.

subjective.question: Why we study marketing?
subjective.answer: Major reason to study marketing is: • Marketing plays an important role in society • It is Vital to business • Marketing offers outstanding career opportunities • Marketing affects your life every day

subjective.question: Why it is said that customer is always right even he is wrong/customer is the king of market?
subjective.answer: 'Putting the customer at the heart of your business planning' sounds simple doesn't it? The truth is, this principle is the cleverest, and also the most startlingly logical strategy for keeping your business at the forefront of its market. The customer is king. This statement is true of every aspect of business. It is the job of everyone in business to please customers - or to enable someone else to please the customer. Without customers, there is no sale. Without satisfied customers, there is no profit. Without delighted customers, there is no repeat business.

subjective.question: How would you define relationship marketing?
subjective.answer: Establishing a long term continuous relationship with the customers initiated and maintained by firm.

subjective.question: What is the difference between mass marketing and database marketing?
subjective.answer: In the data base marketing we have all the relevant information of the target market and we have made the records of the relevant information in the form of the data bases. Mass marketing means the marketing at the large scale marketing in which we do not have the data base form of record of our customer because our target market is very large and the products are produced by the general common character.

subjective.question: What are the objectives of internet marketing?
subjective.answer: The Internet is a very important tool in marketing. The main objectives of internet marketing are: • To reach a large number of consumers quickly and at low cost. • To communicate and interact with customers and build long-term relationships with them. • To provide detailed product information and make buying easy and convenient for customers. • To collect information about customers' needs, wants and buying behavior for better marketing decisions.

subjective.question: What are the 4 Cs of marketing? How do they correspond to the 4 Ps?
subjective.answer: The four Ps of the marketing mix correspond to four Cs from the customer's point of view: • Product corresponds to Customer needs and wants — the solution the customer is looking for. • Price corresponds to Cost to the customer — the total cost the customer bears to obtain the product. • Place corresponds to Convenience — how easy it is for the customer to buy the product. • Promotion corresponds to Communication — a two-way dialogue between the company and its customers.

subjective.question: Explain Business portfolio?
subjective.answer: The business portfolio is a collection of businesses and products that make Up the company. In order to design the business portfolio, the business must: 1) Analyze its current business portfolio and decide which business should receive more, less or no investment. 2) Develop growth strategies for adding new products or business to the portfolio.

subjective.question: Which are the strategies that can be pursued for each Strategic Business Unit (SBU)?
subjective.answer: For each Strategic Business Unit (SBU), the company can pursue one of the following strategies: a) Build: invest more in the business unit in order to build its share, even forgoing short-term earnings. b) Hold: invest just enough to hold the SBU at its current level. c) Harvest: increase the SBU's short-term cash flow regardless of the long-term effect. d) Divest: sell the SBU or phase it out and use the resources elsewhere.

subjective.question: Define the market / product expansion grid?
subjective.answer: 1). Market Penetration 2). Market Development 3). Product Development 4). Diversification

subjective.question: Which factors make the company’s macro environment?
subjective.answer: 1) Demographic 2) Economic 3) Natural 4) Technological 5) Political 6) Cultural

subjective.question: What is mean by Competitive Advantage? How we will design a Competitive Intelligence System?
subjective.answer: To be successful, a company must consider its competitors as well as its actual and potential customers. In the process of performing a competitor analysis, the company carefully analyzes and gathers information on competitors’ strategies and programs. A competitive intelligence system helps the company acquire and manage competitive information. The company must then choose a competitive marketing strategy of its own. The strategy chosen depends on the company’s industry position and its objectives, opportunities, and resources. Some of these are time-tested and some are relatively new .The advantage of our firm with comparison to our competitors which may be in term of low price, high quality, Easy availability of our product, good will, convenience in use etc is included.

subjective.question: What are the key principles for public policy towards marketing?
subjective.answer: a) Full consumer and producer freedom b) Potential harm should be eliminated c) Producer should meet the basic needs of the consumer

subjective.question: Enlist and briefly explain the steps involved in the marketing research process.
subjective.answer: The marketing research process consists of four steps: 1. Defining the problem and research objectives: The marketing manager and the researcher define the problem carefully and agree on the objectives — exploratory, descriptive or causal research. 2. Developing the research plan: Outlining sources of existing data and designing specific research approaches (observation, surveys, experiments), contact methods, sampling plans and instruments for collecting new data. 3. Implementing the research plan: Collecting, processing and analyzing the data. 4. Interpreting and reporting the findings: The researcher interprets the findings, draws conclusions and reports them to management for decision making.

subjective.question: Why do we study consumer behavior?
subjective.answer: Consumers determine the sales and profits of a firm by their purchase decisions. Basic objective of studying consumer behavior is that the firm needs to know how, when, why, and where consumers make purchase decision/ all these are important questions, which are to be known to the companies so that they can design and implement marketing strategies to satisfy the customers.

subjective.question: Explain the five stages of the consumer buying decision process.
subjective.answer: 1. Need recognition: The buyer recognizes a problem or need, triggered by internal or external stimuli. 2. Information search: The consumer collects information from personal, commercial, public and experiential sources. 3. Evaluation of alternatives: The consumer uses the information to evaluate alternative brands on the basis of product attributes and benefits. 4. Purchase decision: The consumer decides which brand to buy; attitudes of others and unexpected situational factors can intervene. 5. Post-purchase behavior: After the purchase, the consumer compares the product's performance with expectations and feels either satisfied or dissatisfied, which affects repeat buying and word of mouth.

subjective.question: In buyer decision process, what are the sources from which buyer can collect information?
subjective.answer: These include personal sources (family, friends, neighbors, acquaintances), commercial sources (advertising, salespeople, dealers, packaging, displays, Web sites), public sources (mass media, consumer-rating organizations), and experiential sources (handling, examining, using the product). The relative influence of these information sources varies with the product and the buyer.

subjective.question: Who are Laggards?
subjective.answer: The people who are suspicious to change and adopt only after the product Has been accepted by the majority

subjective.question: What is market segmentation? Enlist the major bases used for segmenting consumer markets.
subjective.answer: Market segmentation is dividing a market into distinct groups of buyers with different needs, characteristics or behaviors, who might require separate products or marketing mixes. The major bases for segmenting consumer markets are: • Geographic: nations, regions, states, cities, population density and climate. • Demographic: age, gender, family size and life cycle, income, occupation, education, religion, race and nationality. • Psychographic: social class, lifestyle and personality characteristics. • Behavioral: occasions, benefits sought, user status, usage rate, loyalty status and buyer-readiness stage.

subjective.question: List down the chief factors that can be used for segmenting international markets?
subjective.answer: Geographical location Economic factors Political and legal factors Cultural factors

subjective.question: Define business markets?
subjective.answer: The business market includes firms that buy goods and services in order to Produce products and services to sell to others.

subjective.question: Explain the stages of the product life cycle (PLC).
subjective.answer: 1. Introduction: The product is launched in the market. Sales grow slowly, profits are negative or low because of heavy introduction expenses, and promotion aims at creating awareness and trial. 2. Growth: Sales and profits climb rapidly as more buyers accept the product. Competitors enter the market, and the company improves the product and expands distribution. 3. Maturity: Sales growth slows down and profits level off or decline. The market becomes saturated, competition is intense, and the company tries to modify the market, the product or the marketing mix to prolong the stage. 4. Decline: Sales fall off and profits drop. The company may maintain, harvest or drop the product.

subjective.question: What are the main advantages of having brand quality?
subjective.answer: 1) High consumer awareness 2) Easier to launch brand extensions because of high brand credibility 3) A good defense against fair price competition. 4) Customer equity tends to aid marketing planning in assuring loyal customer life time values.

subjective.question: Decision of pricing is very critical for marketers in today's market. Explain the concept of price, write alternate names that can be used for price, and discuss whether pricing applies to profit and non-profit organizations.
subjective.answer: Price is the amount of money charged for a product or service, or the sum of the values that consumers exchange for the benefits of having or using the product or service. It is the only element of the marketing mix that produces revenue; all other elements represent costs. Price is known by many alternate names, for example: rent, tuition fee, fare, toll, rate, interest, premium, salary, tax and charges. While setting prices, the company considers internal factors (marketing objectives, marketing mix strategy, costs and organizational considerations) and external factors (the nature of the market and demand, competition, and economic and government factors). Pricing is used by both profit and non-profit organizations. Non-profit organizations also set prices (such as fees, fares and charges) to recover costs and achieve their social objectives.

subjective.question: When choosing a distribution strategy a marketer must determine what value a channel member adds to the firm’s products. So marketer must assess the benefits received from utilizing a channel partner. Discuss the benefits Offered by Channel Members in detail?
subjective.answer: DISTRIBUTION/MARKETING CHANNEL: Marketing channel or distribution channel is a set of independent organizations who are involved in the process of making the product available to the consumers. Each member in the distribution channel adds a value to the supply chain. Therefore they must be managed well to achieve maximum benefit. Benefits offered by channel members: The channel members offer a number of benefits which are as follows • Information • Matching • Contact • Negotiation • Promotion • Physical distribution

subjective.question: What is the role of broker and agent in the marketing system?
subjective.answer: Main function is to facilitate buying and selling, for which they earn a Commission on the selling price. Generally, specialize by product line or customer Types. BROKERS: Chief function is bringing buyers and sellers together and assisting in negotiation. They are paid by the party who hired them, and do not carry inventory, get involved in financing, or assume risk. Examples: food brokers, real estate brokers, insurance brokers, and security brokers. AGENTS: Represent either buyers or sellers on a more permanent basis than brokers do.

subjective.question: Write down any five reasons of “why would a producer use wholesalers rather than selling directly to consumers or retailers”?
subjective.answer: Quite simply, wholesalers are often better at performing one or more of the following channel functions: • Selling and promoting • Buying and assortment building. • Bulk-breaking • Warehousing • Transportation • Financing • Risk bearing • Market information • Management services and advice

subjective.question: What do you understand by the term Logistics and enlist the logistics functions?
subjective.answer: A value added flows from suppliers to final users Major functions include • Order processing • Warehousing • Inventory Management • Transportation.

subjective.question: Sales promotion is one of the methods of promoting the product in the market. How would you describe it and how many types of Sales Promotion?
subjective.answer: SALES PROMOTION: Sales promotion is offering of short-term incentives to the buyers to purchase a product or use a service. It forces the buyer to do the purchase now. Types of Sales Promotion: There are a total of nine types of sales promotion offers. • Samples: Samples are offers of a trial amount of a product .It is a way to introduce a new product. • Coupons: These are certificates that give buyers a saving when they buy a product. • Premiums: These are goods offered for a free or at a low cost. • Patronage rewards: These are cash or other awards offered for a regular use of a product. • Cash refunds: It is a reduction in price after purchase not at the retail outlet. • Point-of-purchase promotion: In point of purchase promotion a display and demonstration is taken place at the point of purchase. • Advertising specialties: These are useful things on which the name of advertiser is written and given to buyers as a gift. • Price Packs: They offer a saving off the regular price of product. Reduced price is marked by the producer directly on the label. • Contests: Contests give consumer the chance to win something.

subjective.question: Why we use sales promotion tools?
subjective.answer: These can be used to introduce new products, Get existing customers to buy more, Attract new customers, and Combat competition, Maintain sales in off season, Increase retail inventories, Tie in advertising and personal selling, Enhance personal selling efforts.

subjective.question: What do you understand by the term “Communication”, how many element are in communication process. Enlist those elements with a brief explanation.
subjective.answer: Communication: it is a process of sending and receiving messages and getting a response. In communication process there are the following 7 elements. Message: it is the data which sender wants to transmit Media; it is a channel or medium used for communication. For example, internet, phone or letter. Decoding is a process in which the receiver translates the message of sender into its original form. Receiver is the person who receives the sender's message. Response is the reaction of the receiver after he receives the message. Feedback is the message of the receiver to the sender. Noise is the distorted or barriers in the communication process.

subjective.question: What are the steps involved in developing an effective communication?
subjective.answer: Identify the target audience Determine the communication objectives Design a message Choose the media through which to send the message Select the message source Collect the feed back

subjective.question: Which important decisions we should take while developing an advertising program for the product?
subjective.answer: 1 .Setting advertising objectives 2. Setting advertising budgets 3. Developing advertising strategy 4. Message decisions 5. Media decisions 6. Evaluating advertising campaigns

subjective.question: What is meant by reach and frequency?
subjective.answer: Reach is a measure of the percentage of people in the target market who are exposed to the ad campaign during a given period of time. For example, the advertiser might try to reach 70 percent of the target market during the first three months of the campaign. Frequency is a measure of how many times the average person in the target market is exposed to the message. For example, the advertiser might want an average exposure frequency of three.

subjective.question: What is the difference between advertising and publicity?
subjective.answer: An old age says: Advertising you pay for, publicity you pray for. That's because publicity has at least ten times the credibility of advertising. Advertising is a content you pay to present. Publicity refers to free content about you that appears in the media - what others say about you. Publicity can result when an article you write is published, or when information you give to an editor convinces him/her to feature a story about you. Over time, these stories help to create a favorable impression of your product or services.

subjective.question: If you think of your store as a doorway and just on the other side of the doorway is your customer who is reluctant to enter in the shop. How do you get them to come in? You can choose to pull the prospect through the door or you can push them through the door. Explain both concepts (pull marketing and push marketing) with the help of examples.
subjective.answer: Push Marketing A promotion strategy that calls for using the sales force and trade advertising to push the product through the channel is called push marketing. For example the manufacturer promotes the product to wholesalers, the wholesalers promote to retailers and finally the retailers promote to consumers. Pull Marketing A promotional strategy that calls for spending a lot on advertising and consumer promotion to build up consumer demand pull marketing. For example if consumer will ask their retailers for the product, the retailer will ask the wholesalers and wholesalers will ask the producers.

subjective.question: What do you understand by direct marketing; discuss the advantages of direct marketing?
subjective.answer: Direct marketing consists of direct communication with carefully targeted individual consumers to both obtain an immediate response and cultivate lasting customer relationship, with no intermediary levels and is also called one to one marketing. It has been hailed by some marketers as “marketing model of the next millennium”. Advantages It brings so many benefits to both Buyer & Seller which are as follows. Advantages for buyers. • Provides wealth of proportional information. • Greater product access and selection. • Handy, easy & private. • Some companies allow buyers to design their own products online (For example, HP allows customers to make their tailor made notebook online and quotes immediately) Advantages for Sellers. • Because of its one-to-one, interactive nature, the Internet is an especially compelling marketing tool. • Continuous relationships with customers can be developed. • Diminish costs and increase speed and efficiency. • A powerful tool for customer relationship building. • It can also be timed to reach prospects at just the right moment. • The internet is a truly global medium and online marketing offers greater flexibility. • Buyers are now active participants in shaping the marketing offer and process.

subjective.question: E-commerce (electronic commerce or EC) is the buying and selling of goods and services on the Internet, especially the World Wide Web. What do you know about the benefits of using E-Commerce to buyer and seller?
subjective.answer: Benefits of E-Commerce to Buyer: • Easy and private • Convenience • Greater product access • Easy to compare products • Interaction is easy and immediate Benefits of E-Commerce to Sellers • It builds relationship between consumer and seller • Increased speed and efficiency • Flexibility • Access and reach is global • Cost is reduced

subjective.question: Mr. Danish is a marketing head of credit card department at bank UBL. He is interested in establishing a sales force to market the bank Visa card. What do you understand by the term "sales force" and what steps will Mr. Danish take to manage the sales force?
subjective.answer: Sales force: The sales force consists of the people who represent the company to customers and act as a link between the company and its customers. Salespeople prospect for new business, communicate with potential and existing customers, sell and service accounts, and gather information for the company. Steps in managing the sales force: 1. Designing sales force strategy and structure: deciding the size and structure of the sales force and the types of salespeople needed. 2. Recruiting and selecting salespeople: carefully choosing people who are enthusiastic, confident and self-disciplined. 3. Training salespeople: training them about the company, its products, customers and competitors, and in effective selling techniques. 4. Compensating salespeople: deciding the salary, commission, bonus and expenses to attract and retain good salespeople. 5. Supervising and motivating salespeople: directing and motivating them through sales quotas, meetings and incentives. 6. Evaluating salespeople: assessing their performance against standards and taking corrective action.

subjective.question: Retailers may offer one of three levels of service. Describe the types of retailers on the basis of the services they offer.
subjective.answer: On the basis of the level of service they provide, retailers are of three types: 1. Self-service retailers: Customers perform their own locate-compare-select process to save money. Self-service is the basis of all discount operations and is used by sellers of convenience goods (e.g., supermarkets and departmental stores). 2. Limited-service retailers: They provide more sales assistance because they carry more shopping goods about which customers need information (e.g., stores selling appliances and garments). Their increased operating costs are reflected in higher prices. 3. Full-service retailers: Salespeople assist customers in every phase of the locate-compare-select process. They usually carry more specialty goods and slower-moving items, provide services such as credit and merchandise-return privileges, and charge higher prices (e.g., high-end specialty stores and boutiques).

subjective.question: What do you understand by the term micromarketing?
subjective.answer: Micro marketing is the practice of tailoring products and marketing programs to suit the tastes of specific individuals and locations. Micro marketing includes local marketing (Local marketing involves tailoring brands and promotions to the needs and wants of local customer groups—cities, neighborhoods, and even specific stores.
